strings.0: Give a merchant a cart and two trade posts, then mark the honey with an arrow so he carries it over.
strings.2: Trade 10 pieces of furniture with the Frankish village!
strings.3: Load at least 5 sacks of FLOUR onto the ship with a carrier or commander and bring a MERCHANT with a CART aboard!

briefings.10:
You have reached the Saracens' shore.
If you want to go ashore, you will first need to MOOR your ship, because that is the only way your Vikings can embark or disembark, load and unload the ship! 

Select the ship and click the "Moor" button in its display. Then left-click on one of the highlighted places on the shore. 
You can see that a ship is moored because its sails are pulled up.

A ship has its own store, similar to the headquarters and the warehouses, but it is still a means of transport - not a house. Therefore, it is not possible to trade straight from the ship, you need a fixed TRADE POST, i.e. a warehouse.

Your Vikings have already been very busy, they have built a warehouse on the Saracens' shore.
Unload the goods (by selecting the ship and clicking "Unload all" in its "Hold" section), bring the merchant's cart ashore (button "Leave the ship" in the cart's display) and trade with the Saracens!
briefings.12:
Check if you have assigned the northern warehouse to the merchant as trade post A and another warehouse as trade post B, if the merchant drives a cart, and if you have chosen the honey with an arrow in the trade window.

Assign the two warehouses to the merchant!
briefings.01:
THE MERCHANTS

Here are Thorfinn, Lodin and Ari, three experienced merchants. 

When selecting a merchant, his character display shows the TRADE section, where you can adjust the trade settings.

The first thing you have to do is to assign two TRADE POSTS. To do so, click on "Add a trade post" in the TRADE section for every trade post, then click on the respective highlighted building. You can also assign the selected merchant to a trade post by right-clicking the building.
You can trade between any buildings with stores in your own settlement, i.e. also between places of production. 

Assign one merchant to two warehouses.

A merchant only trades while he drives a cart. Right-click the merchant, choose "Assign Vehicle" and click on one of the carts next to the warehouse. Then click the button with the scales ("Set up trade") in the TRADE section, and in the trade window click the arrow next to the honey.
briefings.02:
The merchant only transports the goods you choose in the trade window - in this case honey. 
The merchant starts working by himself once he has two trade posts and a cart. The button with the scales ("Set up trade") in the TRADE section of the merchant's character display opens the trade window.

If you trade within your nation, the trade window shows both trade posts, each with a list of its goods. As long as you don't click on any arrow, the merchant transports nothing. The arrow next to a good shows the direction in which it is taken to the other trade post, and clicking it chooses that good for transport. 
Only the goods you chose with the arrows are transported; you will find them in the "Transfers" list. Clicking an arrow while holding Ctrl balances the stores of that good between both trade posts.
briefings.03:
CLAYME AND STONY NEED TOOLS 
(Trading within your own people)

Somewhere far away from your village your potter and stonemason are doing their jobs. Unfortunately, they forgot to take their good iron tools with them, therefore they are not very productive ... 

Select Thorfinn, Lodin or Ari and assign the northern warehouse as trade post A and the southern warehouse at the pottery as trade post B! (If you want to select a different trade post, click the cross next to the trade post you no longer need in the merchant's TRADE section. Choose another one afterwards.)

Take 5 IRON TOOLS to the warehouse!
briefings.04:
HANDCARTS and OX CARTS

Carts are a major advantage for carriers and merchants, because they can carry 15 and 30 goods respectively at the same time. Therefore, they can make a merchant far more effective. To use a cart, a carrier or merchant must be assigned to the vehicle so he can steer it. 
This can be done using the action button "Assign Vehicle" (right-click the Viking to open his action menu). As soon as you have used this button, the possible vehicles (ship, handcart or ox cart) will light up. Click on one of the carts with the left mouse button to inform the Viking of your choice. 

Hint:
You can also select the Viking and right-click a cart to assign it to him as his vehicle directly.
briefings.05:
GREAT!

Now Clayme and Stony have got their tools, their productivity has been considerably improved.

In the meantime, our merchants can establish new trade relations with the Franks ...
briefings.06:
TRADING WITH ANOTHER NATION

To trade with another nation which has a FRIENDLY attitude towards you, you need an effective trade agreement, and the other people must have a WAREHOUSE. Both prerequisites are fulfilled by this tiny Frankish village on the north coast. Your merchants also need to be assigned a CART.

If you trade with another people, you can choose the goods you want your merchant to trade from among your trading partner's offers. Once the partner's house is one of the trade posts, its offers appear in the merchant's TRADE section, in the "Offer" row. The left-hand side of an offer shows what you give, the right-hand side what you receive in exchange. 
Left-click on the respective offer. Your merchant will then try to trade these goods. 
If you want to choose another trade post, click the cross next to that trade post in the merchant's TRADE section and choose the new trading partner.

Trade 10 pieces of furniture with the Franks! You will receive 20 gold pieces in exchange.
briefings.08:
Let's take a look at the overseas trade. Sometimes you'll need to load ships to take goods to distant countries ... like this friendly Saracen village.

SHIPS are produced in the carpenter's workshop 4. This needs to be built close to the shore so the carpenter can build ships.

Goods are loaded onto a ship by a CARRIER assigned to it or by the ship's commander. You manage the ship's cargo in the "Hold" section of its display: Click on the ship and on the plus sign next to the desired good (add a good that is not listed with "Add a good") to set how much of it should be on board.

Load at least 5 sacks of flour onto the ship and bring a MERCHANT with a CART aboard. (To do so, first assign the merchant a cart as his vehicle, then select the cart, click "Board a ship" in its display and click on the ship.)
briefings.09:
The goods have now been loaded onto your ship and it is ready to set sail!

Any adult Viking assigned to the ship can steer it - he will automatically become its commander! This is done via the action button "ASSIGN VEHICLE". As soon as you have clicked this button, the possible vehicles will light up. Left-click on a ship to inform the Viking about your choice. 
(You can also select the Viking and right-click a ship to assign it to him as his vehicle directly.)

Steer the ship to the Saracens' shore: select it and right-click on the water, as you would send one of your Vikings, or use the "Sail to" button in the ship's display.
